newsitem.title: USA: Colstrip 330 MW unit down, 700 MW unit at 50 pct.
newsitem.headline: Colstrip 330 MW unit down, 700 MW unit at 50 pct.

text.p: The 330 megawatt (MW) unit 1 at the Colstrip coal-fired power plant near Billings, Mont., was still down, while the 700 MW unit 3 was at half capacity, sources familiar with the plant's operations said Monday.
Unit 1 has been out of service since the beginning of January for unplanned work on its cooling tower.
Operations of unit 3 have been curtailed since last weekend, also because of unplanned problems.
Both units are expected to resume full operations sometime this week, the sources said.
Colstrip's other two units, one at 330 MW and one at 700 MW, were said to be operating normally.
Montana Power operates the Colstrip plant and is responsible for the sale of 30 percent of unit 4's output under long-term contracts.

Equity owners include Puget Sound Power and Light Co, Washington Water Power Co, Portland General Electric Co, Pacific Power and Light, and a consortium of GE Credit, Shell Oil Co and a lease-back firm.
